Hi Beth —

Great questions. Summary answers and next steps below; attaching the initial artifacts for your SRE and ML team.

Quick answers:
- Prompt sets: we ship a seeded prompt_set_v1.jsonl (dev/prod labeled). You can add your own canonical prompts; we version them and tie evals to specific prompt_set IDs.
- Regression thresholds: default is a 5% drop in top-1 utility score over the evaluation window, but we can set per-route tolerances (e.g., 3% for billing flows, 7% for internal notes).
- Canary/rollback: canaries run on a configurable percentage of traffic (default 5%). If evaluated metrics breach threshold for 3 consecutive windows, the system triggers automatic rollback and alerts the on-call. Policies are editable in the Console under Deployments -> Rollout policies.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.jsonl, eval_harness_integration_guide.pdf, canary_checklist.md

Proposed next steps:
1) 30m sync Thurs 10:00am PT to walk through the harness integration (Monica will demo).
2) You drop any high-priority prompts into the shared Drive folder.
3) We run a dry canary on a sandbox route next week; we’ll capture metrics in the eval dashboard.

Monica and Rishi are CC'd to provide technical details in thread.

Hi Beth — quick technical follow-up with the integration steps so your SRE can start prepping. Pasted below is a short checklist taken from the attached eval_harness_integration_guide.pdf.

Eval harness integration checklist:
- Create an API key scoped to eva:read and eva:write; store it in your vault.
- Wire a nightly batch job (or on-demand) to POST your labeled ground truth to /evals/upload (JSONL, same format as prompt_set_v1).
- Configure real-time sampling: set sampler to 5% traffic to route /acme/pilot during canary.
- Map output schemas and evaluation metrics (utility_score, exact_match, hallucination_rate).
- Set alert hooks to your PagerDuty integration and a Slack #acme-ai channel.

On regression thresholds: we recommend starting with the default 5% utility_score drop over a 24h rolling window. We'll help craft route-specific thresholds in the Thurs sync.

Short note on prompt sets: prompt_set_v1 includes 120 canonical prompts across 4 intent buckets (billing, customer_info, upsell, general_support). Please add or mark proprietary prompts you want included. Each prompt has an id and a label that the harness uses for per-prompt drift detection.

I uploaded the guide and a sample prompt file to your Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEfAcme-QA

Beth — adding the canary and rollback runbook here (see canary_checklist.md attached). Key excerpts below — please share with your SRE.

Canary runbook (high level):
1) Deploy new model variant to a canary pool (5% traffic).
2) Collect evaluation metrics every 10 minutes for the first 2 hours, then every hour up to 24h.
3) Metrics evaluated: utility_score (primary), latency P95, hallucination_rate.
4) Failure criteria: any of the following over a rolling 3-window:
   - utility_score drop >= configured threshold (default 5%)
   - latency P95 increase > 50ms
   - hallucination_rate uptick > 3 percentage points
5) Automated actions: on failure -> immediate traffic switch to previous stable model; open incident; run a postmortem job that pulls evaluation artifacts into the customer's Drive folder.

Operational notes:
- You can set different thresholds by route via the Console API.
- If you prefer human approval before rollback, set the policy to "manual rollback" and we'll send a Slack + email for a 15m window to approve.

Happy to walk through the canary_checklist during the Thurs sync.

—Rishi
